minutes.headline: Public comment turned into a pitched fight over the FY27 override, staffing cuts, and a disputed Ledger story.
minutes.summary: The bulk of this meeting was public comment: the fire chief, both police and fire union presidents, a school committee member speaking as a parent, and residents disputed a local newspaper's coverage of the FY27 balanced budget, override, and staffing cuts, followed by lengthy rebuttals from board members and the Town Manager. The board also handled routine license and event-permit hearings, a town manager's report, tax-title property and cover-photo votes, committee reports, and voted to enter executive session over opioid-litigation settlement strategy; no vote was taken on the override itself.

what_happened.line: Public comment and board rebuttals covered the FY27 override, staffing cuts, and disputed newspaper coverage, but no vote was taken on the override.
The fire chief and firefighters' union president defended a proposed fourth fire shift, saying the staffing plan has not changed since last July.
The police union president disputed characterizations of town free cash as an available surplus, calling it one-time money for capital needs.
The Town Manager publicly rebutted a newspaper's article point by point on free cash, the deficit, and other disputed claims.
The board tabled a decision on selling two tax-title Hollis Road parcels until members can visit the properties.

why_it_matters: The dispute over budget figures and staffing plans bears directly on how residents weigh the FY27 override at town meeting.
Fire and police staffing levels discussed here affect emergency response coverage funded by the override.
Whether the town sells or keeps the Hollis Road parcels affects future town land use and potential revenue.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every dollar figure and vote outcome that both happened to record — LEAF, fire, health insurance, retirement, budget-cut, and warrant figures all match exactly, as do the three license votes and the cover-photo and Hollis Road decisions. The main things worth checking are: a badly garbled Assistant Town Manager cost figure in our captions (official says ~$145,000), a possible mislabeling of a $3.2M figure as "free cash" when it matches the official's stabilization fund balance, two votes (minutes approval, executive session entry) missing entirely from our minutes, and a town-manager-review "no changes needed" conclusion in ours that the official minutes don't explicitly state.
